correctness.rationale: The exact finite-root-height identity follows from the two-state depth-increment recursion. Infinitely many first-predecessor choices give a unique spine; every off-spine component is a finite chain. The deterministic zero-run/branch formula was reconstructed, including both parity cases, and exact checks confirm it on 4,095 finite eventual-tail trees. The spine label bound sigma_i <= 2i yields the upper union bound sum_i (2i+1) q^(2(i+k)-1). An initial run of 2k-1 penultimate choices gives the matching lower bound. The diameter comparison is an exact tree-path identity, and a maximizing finite tooth is eventually upstream of v_n. No limit claim rests on enumeration; probabilities are over the full i.i.d. infinite attachment law.

originality.rationale: Full text of Tang, Wang and Wu arXiv:2607.02916v1 was inspected, including Sections 1-3 and the trunk/branch derivation. It proves unique-end and infinite-collision properties and gives a branch marginal law, but does not formulate a stabilized diameter-minus-height random variable or its matching tail exponent. Nearby published finite random-tree and generic comb-topology findings were compared by mathematical implications; none in the accessible material provides the exact asserted diameter correction with its Bernoulli-model tail bounds. The deterministic spine argument may have classical antecedents; residual risks are stated.

value.rationale: The difference between the finite-network diameter and the online root-height statistic is a natural exact global metric invariant, not an arbitrary subcase. Eventual pathwise constancy is stronger than asymptotic ratio equivalence, and the q-dependent two-sided tail bound quantifies finite approximation risk. The exponent is optimal via explicit initial long alternating chains. The combination of a deterministic spine-tooth extremal formula and a sharp probabilistic rare-event estimate extends the original collision/branch-geometry problem with a usable geometric result. The formula does not claim the exact prefactor or full distribution.
